title: Predictable Unit Economics: Hero + Battlecard Angles
content:
Goal:
- Create a homepage/hero and product-page messaging bundle that leads with predictable inference costs for engineers while also signalling production-grade reliability and fallbacks. Target: dev/ML engineers evaluating hosted vs managed vs self-hosted inference with sensitivity to latency and cost variance.

Primary thesis / conversion hook:
- Engineering buyers care more about predictable unit economics (cost per useful token/embedding) than raw model FLOPs. If we make predictable unit cost the primary credibility signal and back it with simple microcopy + proof points, we can increase trial-to-paid conversion for both self-serve and SDR-led deals.

Audience slices (short):
- Startup PLG devs: want quick results, low friction, visible cost controls.
- Platform/infra teams at mid-market: require SLA, observability, and ability to pin/bypass models.
- Enterprise compliance teams: private deployments, KMS/HSM, audit logs.

Hero variants (keep short, testable)
- Variant A (Economics-first):
  Headline: "Predictable inference costs, engineered for the product team."
  Subhead: "Ship LLM features with per-call economics you can measure and control—batching, caching, and fallbacks built in."
  Micro CTA: "Estimate my cost" (leads to simple cost estimator modal)
  Rationale: Hooks finance + eng; actionable CTA increases time-on-site and micro-conversions.

- Variant B (Performance-trust):
  Headline: "Latency you can rely on. Costs you can explain."
  Subhead: "SLA-backed serving, fallback model tiers, and cost controls for production LLMs."
  Micro CTA: "See latency profiles"
  Rationale: More signal to infra/platform buyers.

- Variant C (Developer velocity):
  Headline: "From prototype to production—same API, predictable economics."
  Subhead: "One runtime for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments; built-in rollout controls."
  Micro CTA: "Start a free test"
  Rationale: Broad capture—product + engineering.

Hero microcopy / supporting bullets (short, scannable)
- Batching & caching suggestions that cut token cost by up to 3x.
- Auto-fallbacks to quantized variants when capacity tightens—no errors to users.
- Token-level cost breakdowns in Console and a light cost-estimator API you can run locally.

Product page blueprint (sections)
1) Why predictable economics matter (1 paragraph + customer quote).
2) How Redwood controls cost: runtime optimizations, smart routing, auto-batching, KV/prefix cache, quantization profiles.
3) Routing & fallbacks: explain policy types (latency-first, cost-first, region affinity).
4) Proof points & benchmark snippets: p95 latencies, tokens/sec, cost per 1k completion tokens for representative workloads.
5) Integrations & SSO/KMS compliance notes.
6) Pricing snapshot + CTA (cost estimator / contact sales).

Competitive battlecard (TL;DR for landing/product page copy)
- Competitor: Major cloud AI endpoints (Cloud-A, Cloud-B)
  Positioning vs them: they offer easy hosting but opaque unit economics and limited model fallbacks.
  Redwood claim: Transparent token-level billing, automated fallback variants, SLA-backed latency tiers.
  Proof: token-level trace screenshot + sentence about audits.

- Competitor: LLM-API pure-play (Vendor-X)
  Positioning vs them: simple API, broad model catalog, but limited on dedicated/pvt deployments and less tooling for cost control.
  Redwood claim: Same simplicity but with Dedicated and Private deployment options and cost tooling.
  Proof: Dedicated capacity case study snippet (customer X reduced variance by 48%).

- Competitor: Self-hosted runtimes / OSS stacks (OnPrem-LLM, OSSRunner)
  Positioning vs them: full control but heavy ops and long time-to-prod; inconsistent performance across infra.
  Redwood claim: Packaged runtime + orchestration + managed control plane (or private control plane) — predictable ops with less lift.
  Proof: Time-to-production comparison (weeks vs months).

Primary claims (short lines to surface across hero and product page)
- "Predictable unit economics for inference"
- "SLA-backed latency tiers and graceful fallbacks"
- "One API across hosted, dedicated, private"
- "Intelligent batching and cache recommendations—automated win for cost"

Proof points / evidence to collect for page (ask data team / benchmarks)
- p95 latency for 2k token sequence on our hosted G40-equivalent clusters.
- Example: eCommerce summarization workload cost before/after enabling prefix cache.
- A/B test: average monthly spend variance reduction for Dedicated vs Hosted.

CTA & conversion flow experiments
- CTA 1: "Estimate my cost" -> lightbox with workload presets (chat, summarization, embeddings) + sliders for QPS, avg tokens, epoch. Capture email.
- CTA 2: "Run a 24h cost & latency trial" -> allocate sandbox Dedicated slot for 24 hours, auto-ingest small dataset. (For sales-assisted motion)
- CTA 3: "Compare: Redwood vs Self-hosted" -> downloadable 1-pager / battlecard gated behind email.

Microcopy for API/product micro-flows
- API doc snippet headline: "Same API. Predictable Results."
- Endpoint microcopy: "/v1/generate - latency-tier param available; default uses latency-first routing."
- Console label examples: "Token spend (estimated)"; "Batching suggestion"; "Rollback to quantized-variant"

A/B test matrix (prioritized)
- Test 1: Hero variant A (Economics) vs B (Performance) — metric: trial starts (%) and cost-estimator clicks.
- Test 2: CTA wording "Estimate my cost" vs "Get cost projection" — metric: modal opens & email captures.
- Test 3: Add one-line proof under hero vs none — metric: bounce rate & time on page.

Tracking & analytics (implementation notes)
- Tag: hero_variant string, cta_clicked, estimator_completed, sandbox-provisioned, doc-download.
- Funnel: page view -> estimator click -> estimator complete -> trial start -> paid conversion.

Open questions / risks
- Need clear, auditable numbers for our "cost improvement" claims. Ask applied-ml + serving-runtime for canonical benchmark artifacts.
- Legal review for benchmarking language (avoid absolute guarantees unless SLA).
- How to represent Dedicated pricing without showing list prices that complicate negotiations? Consider ranges or "contact sales" for enterprise.

Next steps (owner & timeline)
- Maya: draft first-pass hero A/B creative and push to GH for design review (due in 3 days).
- Priya: pull benchmark artifacts & customer case stats (due in 5 days).
- Liam/Devon: mock up cost-estimator UX and gating flow for sandbox (discuss with infra, due in 7 days).

Appendix: Short copy snippets for quick use
- Social proof line: "Used in production by teams building latency-sensitive features at scale."
- Badge microcopy: "SLA-backed latency tiers" / "Dedicated capacity available" / "Private deployment: VPC & on-prem"
- Footer link label ideas: "How we measure cost" / "Routing & fallback policies"

Notes to reviewers:
- Keep variants short — homepage real estate is limited. Prioritize measurement (we can iterate quickly).
- Prefer claims tied to measurable artifacts (benchmarks, case studies).
- Avoid jargon that non-technical buyers won't follow; but include a developer toggle that surfaces more technical detail for eng reviewers.

[END OF BRIEF]
